attributes.translation: Despite there being no way to guess the winning lottery ticket numbers, some people go out of their way to try and do so every single day. (no chance of being able to)
attributes.nuance_translation: A strong structure which implies that there is almost no chance of doing (A), or that it's impossible. Often following potential verbs.

attributes.body_ja:
「っこない」は接尾（せつび）語（ご）の「っこ」とイ形容詞（けいようし）の「ない」の組（く）み合（あ）わせです。この文型（ぶんけい）が動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）に付（つ）くと、その動詞（どうし）の意味（いみ）に応（おう）じて (A) が不可能（ふかのう）なことを表（あらわ）すイ形容詞（けいようし）になります。

「っこない」は「(A) のはずがない」や「絶対（ぜったい）に (A) はできない」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「っこ」は漢字（かんじ）の「子（こ）」から来（き）ているため、この文型（ぶんけい）は漢字（かんじ）で書（か）かれることがありますが、非常（ひじょう）に稀（まれ）です。
attributes.body:
っこない is a combination of the suffix っこ, and the い-Adjective ない. When attached to the conjunctive form of verbs, it creates new い-Adjectives that express the impossibility of (A). (A) being whichever verb is used.

Common translations of っこない include 'there is no chance of (A)', or 'doing (A) is impossible'.

Caution

Although extremely rare, as っこ stems from the kanji 子（こ）, this grammar point may occasionally be seen in its kanji form.

ようがない・ようもない and っこない both express impossibility, but differ in tone and focus. ようがない・ようもない conveys that there is no way or method to do something, as in 助けようがない (There’s no way to help). っこない is more absolute and emphatic, denying any chance of occurrence, as in 勝てっこない (There’s no way we can win).

attributes.body: っこない and そうにない both indicate improbability, but differ in strength. っこない is categorical and emphatic, rejecting any possibility, as in こんなに弱い選手ばかりでは、勝てっこない (There’s no way we can win with such poor athletes). そうにない is more tentative, suggesting something seems unlikely based on current signs, as in 勝てそうにない (It doesn’t seem like we can win).

attributes.body: Both そうもない and っこない express unlikelihood, but differ in intensity and tone. そうもない implies doubt but leaves room for possibility, e.g. '間に合いそうもない' ('It doesn't seem like we'll make it in time'). っこない is stronger and more absolute, suggesting impossibility, e.g. 'そんなことできっこない' ('There's no way I could do that'). っこない is also more casual and colloquial, while そうもない is more neutral.
